model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy percentages of six different methods evaluated across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with labeled major ticks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, extending to a value past $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)", representing a linear scale ranging from slightly below 40 to above 65, with major tick intervals spaced by 5 units. The "Base" condition is represented by a solid black line with circle markers, demonstrating an increase from a starting value of approximately 38 to a plateau near 44 at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising steadily from an initial value of roughly 40 to end near 48. The "IKE" method is plotted with a solid red line and upward-pointing triangle markers, showing a continuous increase from about 43 to 49. The "MEND" method, designated by a solid brown line with diamond markers, increases from a starting point near 44 to an ending value of approximately 56. The "MEMIT" method is depicted by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, climbing from roughly 43 at the start to finish near 55. The "ROME" method is illustrated by a solid green line with square markers, ascending steadily across the graph from an initial value of approximately 51 to a maximal final value near 66.
